dialect: Standard German as spoken in Germany (everyday colloquial register)

profile.grammar_notes: Modal particles (Abtönungspartikeln) are unstressed words in the middle field (after the finite verb, usually before the object/adverb) that signal the speaker's attitude: shared knowledge, surprise, softening, urging, resignation. They can't start a sentence, are rarely stressed, and don't translate word for word. Most have a second, non-particle job (doch = 'but/yes!', ja = 'yes', denn = 'because', mal = 'times', schon = 'already', eben = 'just/flat'), so each term must be tied to its particle job. Sentence type matters: denn and eigentlich live in questions; mal and doch soften imperatives; ja and doch appear in statements. Combinations (doch mal, ja mal, halt mal) are common. Not a closed set: the core group is ~15 words.
